subject: small submarine
title: What If Your Sub Sank 1,575 Feet? In 1973 Two Men Waited 76 Hours

scenes.text: What if your submarine sank to the seabed with you inside? In 1973, two men found out.
August 29th, 1973, about 150 miles off Cork, Ireland. The rope holding the submersible Pisces Three to its mother ship snaps.
It hits the bottom 1,575 feet down. Inside a sphere six feet across are two British crewmen, one sandwich and one lemonade.
To save oxygen, they stop moving and stop talking. For water, they lick condensation off the walls.
Three days pass. On September 1st, another submersible finally gets a rope onto the hull.
They are hauled up after 76 hours, with 12 minutes of oxygen left. Guinness lists it as the deepest underwater rescue ever achieved.

description:
What if your submersible sank and you had to wait for rescue on the seabed? On 29 August 1973 the Pisces III sank about 150 miles off Cork, Ireland, when the line to its support ship parted. It came to rest 1,575 feet (480 m) down.
Its two British crewmen, aged 28 and 35, spent 76 hours in a sphere six feet across with one sandwich and one lemonade, barely moving or speaking to save oxygen. A rescue line was attached on 1 September. They surfaced with 12 minutes of oxygen left, in what Guinness records as the deepest underwater rescue.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Seventy-six hours, one sandwich, twelve minutes of oxygen to spare. Could you stay that still? What should we run through next?
